title: Segment-level SLA beacons, span-stitching across partial outputs, and redact-as-you-pass telemetry pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Emit lightweight, per-segment (micro-frame) SLA beacons and stitch tracing spans across partial streamed outputs and tool/function calls, while ensuring sensitive content is redacted before telemetry leaves the runtime. This ticket builds a redact-as-you-pass pipeline that tags content for telemetry, applies PII rules and deterministic hashing, and emits segment-level metrics and correlation IDs for downstream analysis.

Background: Current streaming telemetry aggregates at request completion or emits coarse chunk metrics that often lack correlation to tool calls and partial outputs. That makes it hard to attribute latency spikes to the runtime KV cache, model variance, or external tool calls. We need three capabilities: 1) segment-level SLA signals with minimal overhead, 2) deterministic span stitching so a developer can follow a request across model and tool spans, and 3) a privacy-first redaction pass that runs inline to avoid PII leakage to telemetry ingestion.

Scope: Implement runtime hooks that emit 'segment_beacon' events with timing and minimal context, propagate a lightweight correlation GUID across slices, append span-stub events for tool invocation start/finish, and apply a configurable redact pipeline that masks or hashes detected PII in telemetry fields. This work touches the serving runtime, tracer integration, and telemetry ingestion adapters.

Out of scope: Full-text telemetry storage or customer-level unredacted dumps. Detailed post-hoc rehydration of redacted content is intentionally out of scope for this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits a segment_beacon event for at least 95% of streamed segments under normal load with <1ms median extra per-segment CPU overhead
Each streamed request contains a correlation GUID that appears in model spans and tool-call spans so traces can be stitched in the console
Telemetry pipeline applies configured redaction rules and no telemetry payload contains raw email addresses or credit-card-like numbers in test corpus (verified by unit tests)

End-to-end test harness demonstrates tracing a 3-step flow: request start -> model partial output -> external tool call -> final output, with correct span stitching and segment metrics on the dashboard
Feature flag gated with default OFF for existing customers and opt-in for new customers behind runtime-1.23 rollout
design_notes: Event shape: segment_beacon contains: event_type, correlation_guid, segment_index, segment_duration_ms, model_variant, token_count_est, reservoir_sample=false|true (sampling) - only minimal string fields and numeric values in telemetry payloads
Correlation GUID format: 16-byte hex, generated once per high-level request, passed as header through internal runtime APIs and tool-call context

Span stitching: each partial output will emit a span-stub with start_ts and end_ts and correlation_guid; tracer will link parent request span using the same GUID so console stitching is performed by join on correlation_guid

Redact pipeline: three phases - tag, transform, emit. Tagging uses regex + entity models to mark PII. Transform applies masking/hashing rules per tenant policy (mask middle of emails, deterministic SHA256-hash for identifiers). Emit step only includes redacted fields and enumerated safe attributes.
Sampling strategy: Always emit segment_beacon for segments that exceed per-segment latency SLO (configurable), otherwise sample at 1% globally with reservoir sampling tuned by customer traffic tier

Performance trade-offs: Inline redaction adds CPU; we will run redaction on a worker thread pool and fall back to sampled synchronous redaction if under memory pressure. If redact worker queue is full, telemetry will be dropped with a 'telemetry_dropped_reason' metric to avoid request latency impact.

Privacy and compliance: Use deterministic hashing for identifiers so we can correlate across telemetry without storing raw values. Key management considerations: hashing salt per-tenant stored in KMS-managed secret; see security review item.
implementation_plan: 1) Define and document the segment_beacon event contract and correlation_guid propagation in internal tracer API (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2103)
2) Implement correlation GUID propagation in streaming runtime (commit runtime/streaming/correlation, feature branch: feat/seg-beacons)
3) Add span-stub emitters around tool invocation wrappers and model decode loop (ensures tool start/end are recorded)
4) Build redact-as-you-pass pipeline: tagging module (regex + small NER), transform module (mask/hash), and emit adapter mapping to telemetry adapter
5) Integrate with existing tracer backend (OpenTelemetry adapter) and console join logic for trace stitching
6) Add e2e tests in streaming-testkit to validate stitch across a mock external tool and assert redaction on telemetry payloads
7) Rollout behind feature flag: enable in canary runtime pool, collect telemetry_dropped_reason and redact-latency metrics, then gradually increase traffic
8) Security review and KMS secret handling for hashing salt
test_plan: Unit tests for tag rules: edge cases for emails, phone formats, UUIDs
Benchmark redaction pipeline under representative workloads: 1k RPS streaming at p95 segment size, measure CPU and latency delta
Integration test: simulated 3-step flow (model partials + tool call) verifying correlation_guid appears in all spans and in segment_beacon events
Privacy regression: feed synthetic PII corpus and assert none of the raw PII appears in telemetry outputs captured by the ingestion mock
Chaos test: saturate redact worker queue and verify telemetry is dropped with non-blocking behavior and corresponding metric emission
monitoring_and_rollout: Expose metrics: segment_beacon_rate, segment_redact_latency_ms{p50,p95,p99}, telemetry_dropped_reason_total, correlation_guid_miss_rate
Dashboard: per-customer segment latency distribution, fraction of segments that triggered tool-calls, count of stitched traces over time
Alerting: raise if correlation_guid_miss_rate > 0.5% or if segment_redact_latency_ms.p95 > 50ms for >5min
Rollout plan: feature flag ON for internal canary -> 5% customers -> 25% -> 100% with 48h observation windows
Backout: disable feature flag and graceful drain redact worker pool if errors > threshold
